Building the planet…
No. 12 · Volcanoes & Earthquakes

Restless
Earth

The ground under your feet is moving. Earth's crust is cracked into fifteen plates that grind, collide and pull apart, and where they meet, the planet shakes, erupts and sends the sea racing inland. Spin the globe, slice it open and set it off yourself.

  • 15 platesdrifting up to 8 cm a year, about as fast as your fingernails grow
  • 6,371 kmdown to a solid iron core as hot as the Sun's surface
  • VEI 7Tambora, 1815: the largest eruption in recorded history
  • Mw 9.5Valdivia, 1960: the strongest earthquake ever measured
  • 713 km/hhow fast a tsunami crosses the deep ocean
Imagery: NASA Blue Marble · Plate speeds: NNR-MORVEL56 model
